checks.invariant: Authenticated multipart photo ingest must reject or stream-cap each part before allocating the full body in the shared API process, and must enforce a stored-size bound independent of Pillow downscale.
checks.result: save_uploaded_files does await uf.read() with no MAX_PHOTO_BYTES. FastAPI() sets no max body. catalog_limits caps videos and per-lot photo count, not photo bytes. compress_upload_bytes_if_image runs only after the full buffer. Non-image suffixes are stored as-is. Same read pattern is used by POST /jobs/upload, POST /jobs/{id}/upload-files, POST /lots/{id}/photos/upload, and photo replace.

checks.invariant: Video ingest must apply MAX_VIDEO_BYTES before the part is fully buffered, and photo cardinality must be bounded for non-single-lot folder uploads.
checks.result: POST /lots/{id}/videos/upload reads each part fully, then calls lot_video_size_error(len(raw)) (80 MiB). CTBIDS_MAX_PHOTOS_PER_LOT=40 is enforced on /jobs/upload and upload-files only when single_lot_mode is true. Dashboard folder uploads chunk 48 client-side but the API accepts unbounded file lists for batch jobs.

checks.invariant: Multipart filenames cannot escape dest_root, and clients cannot call POST /jobs.
checks.result: save_uploaded_files strips slashes, rejects '..' in Path parts, and relative_to(root) after resolve(). new_batch_dir is UPLOAD_ROOT/account_id/uuid. Clients are allowlisted for /jobs/upload and upload-files, so the unbounded-read path is reachable by the lowest-privilege authenticated role. Filename zip-slip/traversal on this write path is not a candidate.

checks.invariant: Caller-supplied CreateJobRequest.input_folder must be confined to UPLOAD_ROOT/current.account_id, the same chroot _queued_job_upload_folder uses for upload-files.
checks.result: POST /jobs stores payload.input_folder verbatim after only a client-role 403 and sale ownership check. Dashboard Staff server-path control posts that string. upload-files resolves and relative_to(UPLOAD_ROOT/account_id); create_job does not. DELETE /jobs rmtree is chrooted, so the read/catalog path is weaker than delete.

checks.invariant: process_job and /run may rglob and persist only images under the job owner's upload batch, not host paths or other accounts' catalog trees.
checks.result: run_job uses Path(job.input_folder) with no chroot. create_job inserts status=queued; the worker claims any queued row. _process_job_body rglobs IMAGE_EXTS (symlink-following), normalize_job_folder_image may rewrite files in that tree, and _add_catalog_photo copies into catalog/{job.account_id}. Job HTTP access is filtered by ProcessingJob.account_id, which does not bind the filesystem selector.

checks.invariant: R2 job-batch restore keys must use job.account_id, not account/batch parsed from an attacker-chosen path under upload_root.
checks.result: parse_batch_folder takes parts[0], parts[1] from folder.relative_to(upload_root()) and ignores ProcessingJob.account_id (except skipping the literal catalog prefix). ensure_job_input_folder / restore_job_folder_from_r2 then list job-batches/{path_account}/{path_batch}/. Dockerfile.api uses WORKDIR /app and uvicorn from backend, so upload_root is the in-repo backend/data/uploads layout.

checks.invariant: graph_request must not treat a client-controlled string as a full URL that requests.request can fetch, including cloud metadata hosts.
checks.result: url = path if path.startswith('http') else GRAPH_API_BASE+path. Every in-module caller passes a relative path beginning with '/': /oauth/access_token, /debug_token, /me, /me/accounts, /{page_id}/photos, /{page_id}/feed, /{post_id}. Interpolated ids are still prefixed with '/', so they cannot satisfy startswith('http'). No other repository module calls graph_request.

checks.invariant: HTTP/Facebook publishers cannot pass a user URL into graph_request; they must use typed helpers with Graph-relative paths.
checks.result: facebook_page imports exchange/list/upload/feed helpers, not graph_request. facebook_calendar calls delete_page_post and update_scheduled_page_post with stored Graph post ids, which become '/'+post_id. list_user_pages does not follow paging next URLs. No assigned path lets a catalogger supply a full URL into the helper.

candidates.title: POST /jobs stores an un-chrooted input_folder that process_job rglobs into Gemini and the caller's catalog
candidates.description: An authenticated catalogger or owner can POST /jobs with an arbitrary input_folder. Unlike POST /jobs/{id}/upload-files, create_job does not require that path to sit under UPLOAD_ROOT/{account_id}. The row is inserted as queued, so the catalog worker can claim it without a separate unsafe /run trick. process_job then Path.rglob-s image suffixes, may rewrite files in that tree, copies them into catalog/{job.account_id}, and sends them to Gemini. The job row's account_id filter only authorizes who may own the job; it does not isolate the filesystem or R2 batch key. A path equal to the shared upload root or catalog/ subtree therefore selects other tenants' on-disk images. A path shaped as upload_root/{victim_account}/{victim_batch} makes parse_batch_folder restore that tenant's job-batches/ objects using worker R2 credentials.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: CreateJobRequest.input_folder is persisted and later used as a filesystem and R2-namespace selector without the account upload-root chroot that _queued_job_upload_folder already implements, and parse_batch_folder derives tenant from that path rather than from ProcessingJob.account_id.

trace.description: After blocking clients and binding sale_id via _sale_for_user, the handler writes payload.input_folder onto ProcessingJob with status=queued and no UPLOAD_ROOT/account_id relative_to check.
POST /jobs/{id}/run resolves the job by id and account_id, then uses Path(job.input_folder) for R2 staging with no second chroot. create_job already queued the row, so app.worker can also claim it.
account_id and batch_id are taken from the first two path components under upload_root(), not from the job row, then used as the R2 prefix job-batches/{account}/{batch}/.
folder.rglob('*') collects IMAGE_EXTS under the attacker-chosen directory; _add_catalog_photo persists copies under job.account_id and the pipeline sends frames to Gemini.

evidence.description: _queued_job_upload_folder is the sibling control: resolve job.input_folder and relative_to(UPLOAD_ROOT/account_id), used only by upload-files, not by create_job.
delete_job only rmtree when the resolved folder is under UPLOAD_ROOT, so destructive cleanup is chrooted while catalog read is not.
_add_catalog_photo calls persist_catalog_photo(job.account_id, photo_path), copying whatever rglob selected into the caller's catalog namespace.
normalize_job_folder_image writes re-encoded bytes back under job_folder, so a path into another tenant's batch or catalog directory is a write as well as a read.
Dashboard enqueueJob JSON-posts the Staff server-path text field as input_folder, documenting that the API is expected to accept a raw host path.
Image layout is /app/backend/data/uploads (WORKDIR /app, uvicorn from backend), so the upload-root and catalog/ trees are a source-visible absolute layout on API and worker images.

blockers: No OS-enforced empty-allowlist sandbox; hunters must not execute target code, so rglob, R2 restore, persist_catalog_photo, and Gemini were not observed on dummy tenants.
No trusted parent-side scratch promotion procedure, so no local fixture artifact can be retained.

Whether a given Railway worker disk currently holds catalog/{other_account} files, and whether R2 list/get on job-batches/* succeeds for a path-derived other account, is a deployment fact outside this source review.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated dummy two-account fixture with Gemini and R2 mocked, create catalog JPEGs under upload_root/catalog/{B} and a job-batch under upload_root/{B}/{batch}. As catalogger A, insert a ProcessingJob via the create_job request body with input_folder pointing at B's catalog directory and at B's batch directory. Invoke process_job. Confirm A's Photo rows receive B's pixels, B's files may be re-encoded, and restore_job_folder_from_r2 is invoked with job-batches/{B}/{batch}/ rather than A's id. Do not use production data or network.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed: inspect one worker replica's backend/data/uploads/catalog layout after mixed-tenant jobs, and confirm application-side R2 list is not additionally scoped by ProcessingJob.account_id. Do not probe a live customer tenant.

candidates.title: Catalog multipart ingest buffers entire parts in the shared API process with no photo byte cap
candidates.description: Restricted clients and staff upload photos through POST /jobs/upload and POST /jobs/{id}/upload-files into save_uploaded_files, which await-reads each UploadFile fully, optionally runs Pillow, writes the bytes, and mirrors to R2. catalog_limits defines MAX_VIDEO_BYTES and a 40-photo CTBids cap, but no photo-byte ceiling, and the 40-file cap applies only in single_lot_mode. Lot video upload does have an 80 MiB cap, but only after the entire part is already in memory. FastAPI is constructed with default options (no request-size limit in source). Concurrent saves use a semaphore of 12, so several large parts occupy RAM together on the single API process that also serves other tenants' dashboard and pool checkouts.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Multipart handlers treat UploadFile.read() as the size gate: photos never have a byte budget, and videos check MAX_VIDEO_BYTES only after the full buffer exists. There is no source-visible Starlette/FastAPI max body, per-request file-count cap for batch jobs, or streaming discard.

trace.description: Authenticated client or catalogger posts files: list[UploadFile] with no length or byte Form constraint; CTBIDS_MAX_PHOTOS_PER_LOT applies only when single_lot_mode is true.
body = await uf.read() materializes the entire part. concurrency=12 gather runs many such reads. Pillow compress runs after this allocation; non-image names skip compress and keep raw bytes.
target.write_bytes(body) plus mirror_local_file_to_r2 retain the object on local disk and operator-owned R2. The same process hosts other tenants' HTTP and QueuePool.

evidence.description: MAX_VIDEO_BYTES is the only ingest byte constant; there is no MAX_PHOTO_BYTES. CTBIDS_MAX_PHOTOS_PER_LOT is a listing count, not a transfer-size cap.
upload_lot_videos does raw = await file.read() then lot_video_size_error(len(raw)), so the advertised 80 MiB bound is after unbounded buffering.
app = FastAPI(title=settings.app_name) installs no max request size, body limit, or upload middleware.
client_http_allowed includes POST /jobs/upload, so the unbounded buffer is reachable by the client role, not only owners.
UPLOAD_FILE_CHUNK = 48 is a browser timeout workaround, not an API cardinality or byte limit; additional chunks append to the same job.

blockers: No sandbox or target execution, so peak RSS and disk growth were not measured with a small oversized fixture.
Railway/proxy/client_max_body_size and platform multipart limits are not declared in this repository; an upstream cap would change shared impact and must be owner-observed.
Paid R2 put and Gemini spend from a huge accepted batch were not exercised (mocked-only local check required).

validation_plan.local: With Gemini and R2 mocked and strict process memory/time limits, post one oversize JPEG and one oversize non-image part to save_uploaded_files / create_job_from_upload, and one oversize video to upload_lot_videos. Observe that photo parts are fully buffered with no 413, and that video rejection happens only after len(raw) is known. Repeat with a large files list while single_lot_mode is false. Do not stress a shared host beyond the fixture limit.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed: record whether Railway/ingress enforces a request body ceiling in front of the API service, and whether that ceiling applies to multipart parts before uvicorn allocates them. Do not flood the production API.

hardening: graph_request should ignore or reject any path that is not relative to GRAPH_API_BASE (including startswith('http')), even though current callers only pass /me-style paths; requests.request follows redirects by default.
Reuse _queued_job_upload_folder (or equivalent) inside create_job, and compare parse_batch_folder's path account_id to ProcessingJob.account_id before R2 list/get.
process_job error_message embeds the resolved folder path ('Input folder not found: {folder}'), which in non-production JobOut already returns full paths via public_job_input_folder.

save_uploaded_files filename chroot (reject '..', relative_to after resolve) is the right write-side pattern; pair it with a streaming byte ceiling and a batch file-count cap even when single_lot_mode is false.
Video MAX_VIDEO_BYTES should be enforced while streaming the part, not after await file.read().
Path.rglob follows directory symlinks; even after a chroot, listing should not follow links out of the batch directory.
